Problem

  • Hidden theme copies are not downloaded; stills are lossless WebP; the home page is under 700 KB at 375 px.

## Problem

Reporters in any language but German get English. TEXT lives in code (issue_assistant.py:1563-1706); the schema enums `choice(["en", "de"])` (:1223, :1240), `issue_language` (:871), `detect_language` with GERMAN_WORDS/ENGLISH_WORDS (:146-155, :859-863), `format_date` with MONTHS_DE (:156-159, :884-887) and prompts/rules.md:17 all hard-code the two languages. Adding a language means touching schema, date and detection code, and no test keeps en and de complete today: a key added only to English raises KeyError for German reporters at runtime (the closed-unanswered, closed-duplicate and German line-link texts have no German test). Dosu, gh-aw and CodeRabbit answer in the reporter's language.

## Proposal

1. Move the texts into `locales/<code>.toml` (tomllib, standard library only per ADR 0003), each with texts, a date format, month names and stopwords; ship en and de plus machine-drafted fr, es, pt, it and nl. `LANGUAGES = tuple(sorted(TEXT))`.
2. Schema `language` = enum of the locales plus "other" (English headings, prose in the reporter's language); prompts/rules.md gets the list through a `{languages}` placeholder: "answer in the reporter's language; set language to its code if listed, otherwise other".
3. Store the language in the marker (`<!-- issue-assistant:analysis lang=fr ... -->`, MARKER already supports attributes) and have `issue_language()` read it first, so sweep texts need no AI.
4. Dates per locale from the catalog (ISO 8601 fallback).
5. The parity test (IA-TEST-06) and README "Languages" with how to contribute a catalog; CHANGELOG `### Added`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Seven locales ship; adding one is one TOML file plus nothing else.
- Parity, marker and detection tests pass; 100 % coverage; REUSE lint passes.

## Evidence

- issue_assistant.py:146-159, :859-887, :1223, :1240, :1563-1706; prompts/rules.md:17; parity of en/de keys and placeholders checked today but not enforced (code-core and tests lenses).

What happens

test_a_commonmark_parser_finds_no_definition_in_what_the_engine_reads in tests/test_properties.py fails in the long search that tests/conftest.py describes. On main (7e14dd8), pytest -m hypothesis --hypothesis-profile=nightly --hypothesis-seed=N -k commonmark_parser_finds_no_definition fails for the seeds 5, 17, 24 and 28 of the seeds 1 to 40. The CI passes because its profile ci is derandomized. The nightly Property tests workflow runs the smaller profile local and has stayed green.

Two of the causes are in the oracle of the tests, and they are what this issue is about. A third is in the cleaning itself and has its own report.

1. The oracle reads definitions that GitHub shows

The parser of tests/oracle.py, markdown-it-py 4.3.0, reads a definition in these texts, where GitHub shows text:

Text markdown-it GitHub
'[0]:\n=' definition, destination = <h1>[0]:</h1>
'[x]:\n=\n"hidden"' definition, title hidden <h1>[x]:</h1> and <p>"hidden"</p>
'[0]:\n--' definition, destination -- <h2>[0]:</h2>
'[0]: /u "a\n=\nb"' definition, title a\n=\nb <h1>[0]: /u "a</h1> and <p>b"</p>
'[a\nb]:\n=' definition a b a heading
'[0]:\\\t0' (a backslash and a tab) definition <p>[0]:\ 0</p>

Its block rule reference reads the destination and the title over the rows that follow, also over a row that underlines a setext heading. In CommonMark that row ends the paragraph first, and the definitions are read from the rows above it. Underlines of - and --- don't show this, because the rules for list items and thematic breaks end the definition first. -- does show it.

Its parseLinkDestination takes a backslash before any character as an escape, so it swallows the tab. A destination without <> holds no space and no ASCII control character, and a tab is one. markdown-it already stops at a backslash before a space. The cleaning is right for all of these texts: it keeps them, as GitHub shows them.

2. markdown-it-py crashes

MarkdownIt("commonmark").parse('>- <!A\n>') and parse('> - <!--\n>') raise IndexError: string index out of range in StateBlock.getLines. With a line feed at the end, both parse. Seed 24 hits this.

What should happen

  • The Parser of tests/oracle.py reads definitions as GitHub does, next to its overrides of normalizeLink and validateLink. Each correction gets a comment that says what GitHub does:
    • A definition never runs over a row that underlines a setext heading, with = or -. A lazy row is no underline, so the oracle keeps reading a definition over it, as GitHub does.
    • In a destination without <>, a backslash before a space, a tab or a line feed is no escape.
    • It parses a text with a line feed added at its end, so the crash doesn't reach the tests. A final line feed changes nothing in CommonMark.
  • test_a_commonmark_parser_finds_no_definition_in_what_the_engine_reads gets a @hypothesis.example for each text above that it can judge, so the derandomized CI tries them on every run.

I rejected these alternatives:

  • Taking the texts of part 1 out in shown_text: the AI would lose words that a reader sees.
  • hypothesis.assume to skip such inputs: the test would no longer look at the corners where a definition hides.
  • Derandomizing the local profile: the random search would stop finding what it is there to find.

What must not break

  • Every other example of the test still passes, including [x]: <> "hidden", `[x]: #
    "hidden
  1. hidden"and[x]:
    /url "hidden"`, which GitHub reads as a definition and the cleaning takes out.
  • [x]: /url === stays a definition followed by the paragraph ===, as on GitHub, and '[0]: =' stays as it is in the cleaning.
  • The other users of the oracle (problems, headings) keep their results, and the coverage of issue_assistant stays whole.

How to test it

  • The new examples of the property test fail on main and pass with the fix.
  • pytest -m hypothesis --hypothesis-profile=nightly --hypothesis-seed=N -k commonmark_parser_finds_no_definition passes for the seeds 5, 17, 24 and 28, once the cleaning is corrected as well.

## Problem
The update PR body (`blueprint-update.yml:129-133`) reads only "Brings the repository from the blueprint's vA to [vB](…) with `copier update`." There is no compare link, no list of changed files, no conflict instructions, no note that it merges itself (and how to stop that), and when releases are skipped (v0.9.1 → v0.10.1) the notes of the intermediate release (v0.10.0) never appear. Renovate's PRs always carry release notes.

## Proposal
`blueprint.py update-body BEFORE AFTER [--conflicts FILE...]` in `blueprint/update.py` renders: for each tag in (before, after] (`gh release list` / `gh release view --json body`, source repo from `_src_path`) a `<details><summary>vX.Y.Z</summary>` with the curated part of the notes; `Compare: <src>/compare/BEFORE...AFTER`; the changed files as a list; conflicts as a task list `- [ ] path` with "resolve the <<<<<<< markers on this branch, then push"; and the footer "Merges itself once every check passes; set the repository variable BLUEPRINT_AUTOMERGE to off to review every update." Truncate to GitHub's 65,536-character limit. The workflow uses it for create and edit. CHANGELOG (Added).

- Every update PR shows the notes of all releases it brings, a compare link and the changed files.
- Conflicting updates explain how to resolve them.

The Rollout took the release of v1.3.0 for no release: the plan of run [41294123263](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/actions/runs/41294123263) wrote "The run made no release", skipped every repository and ended green, although the run of the Release workflow published v1.3.0. No repository got its update pull request until the blueprint bots were started by hand.

**Why:** the release was made during the hour that repeats when the clocks of the US go back (2026-11-01, 08:00 to 10:00 UTC). GitHub then dates things inconsistently: the job *publish the release* was created at 09:12:15, before the start of its own run at 09:24:36. The plan asks for `actions/runs/<id>/jobs`, whose default `filter=latest` leaves that job out, so it found no job that published anything:

```console
$ gh api "repos/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/actions/runs/41288744162/jobs?per_page=100" --jq '.jobs[].name' | grep -c publish
0
$ gh api "repos/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/actions/runs/41288744162/jobs?filter=all&per_page=100" --jq '.jobs[].name' | grep -c publish
1
```

**Fix:** ask with `filter=all` and take the job of the last attempt, so that a run that GitHub started again still counts by its last attempt.

## What happens

The report of flaky tests (the job *report the flaky tests* of `.github/workflows/after-checks.yml`) reads the log of each job that failed at first to find the tests that pytest names, and the step and error of other tests. Since GitHub CLI v2.97.0, `gh api` refuses to print a raw answer that contains terminal escape sequences, and prints instead:

```
the response contains terminal escape sequences; pass --allow-escape-sequences to output it anyway
```

with exit code 1. Every log of GitHub Actions carries escape sequences, the colors of the commands that a step runs. The step sends the errors of that download to `/dev/null` and runs without `pipefail`, so the log comes back empty and the report names no test, without any word of why.

## Evidence

- The release notes of [gh v2.97.0](https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.97.0) (GHSA-3m3g-3wcr-px46): `gh api` no longer prints externally controlled content with escape sequences. Since then a raw body that isn't JSON goes through a guard, and only `--allow-escape-sequences` lets it through.
- The image of `ubuntu-24.04` (20261101) brings GitHub CLI 2.103.3.
- Locally with gh 2.102.0: `gh api repos/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/actions/jobs/128885642907/logs > log` writes 0 bytes and exits 1 with the message above; with `--allow-escape-sequences` it writes the 71 KB log, with 42 lines of escape sequences.
- The report of 2 November 2026 in Dennis-Otto/homedarts-for-autodarts#586 shows `–` as the test of `check (home-assistant)`, although the log of that job ([125020429633](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/homedarts-for-autodarts/actions/runs/41364080290/job/125020429633)) names `FAILED tests/test_stuck_hand.py::test_a_hand_that_comes_back_within_a_minute_gets_no_second_restart`. The other reports of the fleet since then show `–` there as well.

## What should happen

- The download passes `--allow-escape-sequences` when `gh help api` lists the option, and leaves it out for an older gh, which knows no such option.
- A log that can't be read gives a warning in the run, with gh's reason, rather than an empty log without a word.
- The other `gh api` calls of the blueprint's workflows and scripts that download raw text are checked for the same problem.

`.github/download.sh` runs each call of gh through `tried()`, which tries a failed call again up to five times. It keeps the errors of each try in a file of their own, but the standard output of every try, the failed ones too, goes straight into the output of `tried()`.

Without a pinned sha256, the script reads the digest of the asset that GitHub keeps:

```sh
digest="$(tried gh api … "repos/$repository/releases/tags/$tag" --jq ".assets[] | … | .digest // \"\"")"
```

When GitHub answers with an error, `gh api` writes the raw body of the response to its standard output, even with `--jq`. So when the first try gets, say, a 502 with a JSON body and the second try works, `digest` holds the body of the error followed by the digest. It no longer matches `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`, and the download fails with "GitHub keeps no sha256 of …", although the retry worked: exactly the outage that the retries are there for (decision 0133) turns into a red check with a wrong explanation.

**Expected:** the output of a failed try is dropped; `tried()` prints only the output of the try that succeeded.

**Fix:** write the standard output of each try into a file of its own and print it only on success. A test with a fake gh that answers an error body on its standard output first and the digest on the second try.

Found while looking into the flaky end-to-end tests of paperless-unified-search.

`tests/test_downloads.py::test_a_download_that_stalls_is_tried_again` fails now and then on a loaded machine, as two agents of the run found while they ran `scripts/check.sh` on Windows.

## What happens

The test runs `.github/download.sh` with `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT=1`: the stand-in of gh stalls on its first call, `timeout` ends that call after a second, and the second call downloads the asset. But the limit of one second holds for every call, the second one too: on a loaded machine, the stand-in of gh, a bash script that starts four more programs, takes longer than a second, and the call that should download the asset is ended as well. The script then tries five times and fails with the outage of GitHub.

On `main` (4b623985), with the test run many times at once on a machine with 32 logical cores:

| Runs at once | Failed |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | 0 |
| 8 | 0 |
| 16 | 0 |
| 24 | 9 |
| 28 | 28 |

Each failure is the same: `GitHub didn't answer in 1 seconds.` five times, and the exit code 1.

## Expected

The test passes however slow the machine is: no call that should work runs against a limit that a slow machine can miss, and the test doesn't wait seconds for a limit either.

## What happens

The website of the blueprint and of every repository made from it is built with MkDocs and Material for MkDocs:

- `stacks/docs/requirements-docs.in:10-13` asks for `mkdocs-material[imaging]`, `mkdocs-glightbox`, `mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin` and `mkdocs-static-i18n`.
- `stacks/docs/requirements-docs.txt:516` pins `mkdocs==1.6.1`, line 535 `mkdocs-material==9.8.0`.
- `.github/mkdocs_blueprint.py` holds 2,602 lines of MkDocs hooks (`on_config`, `on_files`, `on_page_markdown`, `on_page_content`, `on_post_page`, `on_post_build`, `on_post_template`, `on_page_context`, `on_nav`), and `.github/mkdocs-blueprint.yml` uses the plugins `search`, `privacy` and `social` of Material.

Upstream has ended the development of both:

- <https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2025/11/05/zensical/> says: "Material for MkDocs is in maintenance mode. Feature development has ended. We will continue fixing critical bugs and security vulnerabilities through May 5, 2027, when upstream maintenance ends." The home page of the theme shows "End of life on May 5, 2027".
- The same article says that "MkDocs must be considered a supply chain risk, since it's unmaintained since August 2024." PyPI confirms it: the latest release of `mkdocs` is 1.6.1, and after it there are only `2.0.dev` releases (2.0.dev6 the newest).

The repository says nothing about it: `grep -rli zensical` over the Markdown, YAML, Python, TOML, Jinja and JSON5 files finds nothing, no decision in `docs/decisions/` names the end date, no rule of Renovate holds `mkdocs` below 2 on purpose, and no issue plans a move.

From May 2027 a vulnerability or a break in the theme or in MkDocs 1.6, such as one by a new release of Python, Pygments or Python-Markdown, gets no fix upstream, for every website of the fleet at once. Neither successor is a bump that Renovate brings: the hooks, the i18n setup, the social cards, the privacy plugin and the accessibility check are written against MkDocs 1.x and Material 9, so a move needs a plan, and six months is not much for that amount of code.

## What should happen

A record of decision in `docs/decisions/` names the end date and decides between the options: stay on the last release of Material and MkDocs 1.6 and accept the risk for a stated time, move to Zensical (the successor that the authors of Material name and call compatible with existing MkDocs projects), or move to another generator. Its base is a list of what the websites need today, one line for each hook of `.github/mkdocs_blueprint.py` and each plugin of `.github/mkdocs-blueprint.yml` and `stacks/docs/requirements-docs.in`, with what each option offers for it.

Until the decision is carried out, a rule in `.github/renovate-blueprint.json5` and `template/.github/renovate-blueprint.json5.jinja` keeps `mkdocs` below 2 with its reason in a comment, so that a stable MkDocs 2.0 does not arrive as a routine pull request, and an issue with a date tracks the move itself.

  • stacks/docs/requirements-docs.in:10-13 asks for mkdocs-material[imaging], mkdocs-glightbox, mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin and mkdocs-static-i18n.
  • stacks/docs/requirements-docs.txt:516 pins mkdocs==1.6.1, line 535 mkdocs-material==9.8.0.
  • .github/mkdocs_blueprint.py holds 2,602 lines of MkDocs hooks (on_config, on_files, on_page_markdown, on_page_content, on_post_page, on_post_build, on_post_template, on_page_context, on_nav), and .github/mkdocs-blueprint.yml uses the plugins search, privacy and social of Material.

Upstream has ended the development of both:

  • https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2025/11/05/zensical/ says: "Material for MkDocs is in maintenance mode. Feature development has ended. We will continue fixing critical bugs and security vulnerabilities through May 5, 2027, when upstream maintenance ends." The home page of the theme shows "End of life on May 5, 2027".
  • The same article says that "MkDocs must be considered a supply chain risk, since it's unmaintained since August 2024." PyPI confirms it: the latest release of mkdocs is 1.6.1, and after it there are only 2.0.dev releases (2.0.dev6 the newest).

The repository says nothing about it: grep -rli zensical over the Markdown, YAML, Python, TOML, Jinja and JSON5 files finds nothing, no decision in docs/decisions/ names the end date, no rule of Renovate holds mkdocs below 2 on purpose, and no issue plans a move.

From May 2027 a vulnerability or a break in the theme or in MkDocs 1.6, such as one by a new release of Python, Pygments or Python-Markdown, gets no fix upstream, for every website of the fleet at once. Neither successor is a bump that Renovate brings: the hooks, the i18n setup, the social cards, the privacy plugin and the accessibility check are written against MkDocs 1.x and Material 9, so a move needs a plan, and six months is not much for that amount of code.

What should happen

A record of decision in docs/decisions/ names the end date and decides between the options: stay on the last release of Material and MkDocs 1.6 and accept the risk for a stated time, move to Zensical (the successor that the authors of Material name and call compatible with existing MkDocs projects), or move to another generator. Its base is a list of what the websites need today, one line for each hook of .github/mkdocs_blueprint.py and each plugin of .github/mkdocs-blueprint.yml and stacks/docs/requirements-docs.in, with what each option offers for it.

Until the decision is carried out, a rule in .github/renovate-blueprint.json5 and template/.github/renovate-blueprint.json5.jinja keeps mkdocs below 2 with its reason in a comment, so that a stable MkDocs 2.0 does not arrive as a routine pull request, and an issue with a date tracks the move itself.

## Texts

### Integration: `custom_components/autodarts/translations/de.json`

#### [`config.progress.wait_for_device`](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/ha-autodarts/blob/main/custom_components/autodarts/translations/de.json#L96) · outdated

English now:
```text
Open [Autodarts login]({verification_uri_complete}) and approve the connection. Alternatively, open [{verification_uri}]({verification_uri}) on another device and enter **{user_code}**.

This screen continues automatically after approval. Only enter this code in your own Autodarts login.
```

English when last translated:
```text
Open [Autodarts login]({verification_uri_complete}) and approve the connection. Alternatively, open [{verification_uri}]({verification_uri}) on another device and enter **{user_code}**.

This screen continues automatically after approval. Only share this code with your own Autodarts login.
```

German now:
```text
Öffne die [Autodarts-Anmeldung]({verification_uri_complete}) und bestätige die Verknüpfung. Alternativ kannst du [{verification_uri}]({verification_uri}) auf einem anderen Gerät öffnen und **{user_code}** eingeben.

Nach der Freigabe geht es hier automatisch weiter. Gib diesen Code nur bei deiner eigenen Autodarts-Anmeldung ein.
```

#### [`entity.sensor.favourite_double.name`](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/ha-autodarts/blob/main/custom_components/autodarts/translations/de.json#L311) · outdated

English now:
```text
Favorite double
```

English when last translated:
```text
Favourite double
```

German now:
```text
Lieblingsdouble
```

### Cards: `TEXT.de` in `custom_components/autodarts/frontend/autodarts-card.js`

#### [`heatmap_label`](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/ha-autodarts/blob/main/custom_components/autodarts/frontend/autodarts-card.js#L1071) · outdated

English now:
```text
Dartboard colored by how often each bed was hit
```

English when last translated:
```text
Dartboard coloured by how often each bed was hit
```

German now:
```text
Dartscheibe, eingefärbt nach Trefferhäufigkeit je Feld
```

## How to help

You need a GitHub account, but no programming and no setup: it all happens in the browser.

1. Open the file and click the pencil, *Edit this file*. GitHub makes a copy of the repository for you, a fork.
   - [`custom_components/autodarts/translations/de.json`](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/ha-autodarts/edit/main/custom_components/autodarts/translations/de.json) for the texts of the integration: setup, entities, actions and messages
   - [`custom_components/autodarts/frontend/autodarts-card.js`](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/ha-autodarts/edit/main/custom_components/autodarts/frontend/autodarts-card.js) for the texts of the dashboard cards, in the block `de: {` of `const TEXT = {`
2. Find each key listed above, whose link shows its line, and change only the text in quotes. Keep the key, the quotes, a comma after them, placeholders such as `{name}`, and the order of the lines.
3. Click *Commit changes…*, then *Propose changes* and *Create pull request*. A title such as `fix(i18n): update the German texts` fits. The checks of the pull request test every language, and a maintainer helps when one fails.
4. Once it is merged, the next release brings your texts to every user, and the [changelog](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/ha-autodarts/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) thanks you by your GitHub name. A maintainer writes that line, you don't need to.

Is a text still right as it is? Say so in a comment here, or put a line such as `Translations-checked: de config.progress.wait_for_device` with its keys into the description of your pull request; once merged, the bot counts them as up to date.

The [translation guide](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/ha-autodarts/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#translations) has the style of each language: how to address the reader and which darts terms stay English. This issue updates itself when the texts change and closes itself once every German text is up to date.

## What happens

In the list of the administration settings every section shows a black icon; the entry of Paperless Sync shows the logo of the app in green and blue (Nextcloud 33, light theme, seen on a phone). Paperless Unified Search, right below it, has a black icon, as the sections of Nextcloud itself do.

- `lib/Settings/AdminSection.php:38` returns `img/app.svg`, the colored logo.
- `img/app-dark.svg`, the file that the apps of Nextcloud keep as the black version for light backgrounds, is the same colored picture (fills `#0082c9`, `#1f8f72` and `#daf4ec`), so the filter of the activity settings (`lib/Activity/Filter.php:40`) shows it in color as well.
- In the dark theme Nextcloud inverts the icons of these lists, which turns the colors of a colored icon into wrong ones.

## What should happen

The section, and every other place where Nextcloud shows a one-colored icon of an app (the lists of the settings, the activity filter and its entries, notifications, the Flow operation), gets a black icon of the app, `img/app-dark.svg`, in the weight of Nextcloud's own icons, as Paperless Unified Search has it. It turns white by itself in the dark theme. The colored logo stays where a logo belongs: the App Store, the website and the README.

A test that the section returns the black icon and that `img/app-dark.svg` holds no color, and the screenshots of the settings anew.

texts.source:
## Problem

- The home page loads 29 resources, 1,893 KB. In the light theme the four dark PNGs (≈ 499 KB) are downloaded as well, because all 11 images load eagerly and without width or height (`docs/index.md:62-95`), which also shifts the layout.
- `search-and-open.gif` is 397 KB, 57 frames, 12.29 s, loops forever and can't be paused (WCAG 2.2.2), and renders 328 px wide on a phone. Its first frame (1.6 s, also what still renderers show) is only the file list; the Paperless results appear at frame 40 for 2.6 s. It has no dark version.
- The PNGs are not optimized (01: 175 KB, 03: 185 KB).

## Proposal

1. `docs/index.md`: `{ loading=lazy width="1600" height="900" }` on every screenshot (phone ones 780×1688), so hidden-theme images are never fetched. If `rb-website-a11y-perf` adds lazy loading in the shared hook first, keep only the dimensions.
2. `tests/e2e/screenshots.mjs`: the animation starts with a 1.5 s results frame (also the poster), draws a 3 px outline around the "Paperless documents" group in the results frame, and also writes `search-and-open-dark.gif` and a WebM (Playwright's `recordVideo` or the frames encoded in the Playwright image). README uses `<picture>` with `prefers-color-scheme` for the two GIFs.
3. Website hero (`docs/overrides/home.html`, `template: home.html` in the front matter of index): logo, tagline and two calls to action next to `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline controls preload="metadata" poster="…/01-unified-search.png">`; under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` only the poster; under 600 px the phone screenshot via `<picture>`.
4. An oxipng/pngquant pass in `scripts/screenshots.sh` (in Docker).
5. Target: under 700 KB first load on the home page.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The home page transfers under 700 KB on first load in either theme and fetches no hidden-theme image.
- [ ] The hero animation can be paused, respects reduced motion, starts on the results and has a dark version.
- [ ] Pictures come only from the screenshot script.

## Evidence

- Docs-UX lens measurements on the live site (2026-10-12): 29 requests, 1,893 KB, DOMContentLoaded 295 ms; GIF frames `gif-frame-00.png` and `gif-frame-40.png`, `site-home-mobile-light.png` (F:/IdeaProjects/.night/scratch/screens/paperless-unified-search/).
- `docs/index.md:62-95`; `README.md:16` (hero GIF), `:45`.

## Update (2026-10-25)

Measured again on the live site in a fresh Chromium: the blueprint's hooks now load every picture but the first lazily, so the screenshots of the other theme no longer load. The home page still transfers 865 KB in the light theme and 882 KB in the dark one, in 23 requests, and the GIF is 396 KB of it, almost half. The website loads it from `raw/main`, so it can't show a video in its place, and none of the screenshots of the gallery have a width and a height.

texts.source:
## What happens

A user can save up to ten searches for the notifications about new documents, but a notification reads only "New in Paperless: <title>" or "<n> new documents in Paperless" with the titles. `lib/Notification/Notifier.php:65-72` builds the subject of one document from the document alone:

```php
$subject = $l->t('New in Paperless: {document}');
```

and lines 76-88 the one of several from their titles. The search that matched is not kept: `NewDocumentAlerts` stores `['count' => ..., 'documents' => $documents]` as the parameters of the subject (`lib/Service/NewDocumentAlerts.php:406`), each document with its title, the ID of its file and its path, and `Notifier::documentsOf()` (lines 97-108) reads only these three. No text of the catalogs in `l10n/` names a search in a notification.

A user with `tag:unpaid` and `correspondent:"tax office"` so can't tell why a document was announced or which notification is the urgent one, and a search that matches too much can't be found and corrected from its notifications. The more searches a user saves, the less the notifications say.

## What should happen

`NewDocumentAlerts` knows which term found which document (`findTerms()` answers the IDs per term, lines 291-335, and lines 341-352 join them per user). It stores the first term that matched with each document of a notification, and `Notifier` shows it as the message of a notification about one document, such as "Found by your search tag:unpaid"; a document that only **Every new document that I can open** found gets no such line. A notification that was stored without the field stays readable.

Tests belong in `NotifierTest` and `NewDocumentAlertsTest`, and the new text in the seven catalogs of `l10n/`.

Found by the audit of 2026-11-11 (pus-features-6).
